title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Grothendieck is studying a group M = N_{1,1}~ of 'arithmetic' automorphisms of the profinite modular tower. He writes it as M ≃ Γ_Q~·𝔊^+, an extension of (a variant of) Gal(Q̄/Q) by 𝔊^+ = SL(2,Z)^, acting by conjugation/outer action. Inside SL(2,Z)^ he fixes the standard torsion elements: ρ of order 3 (or 6) and σ of order 4, with σ² = −1.

The subgroups. For u ∈ M he defines the 'normalizer' subgroups
- N*_ρ = {u : u(ρ) = ρ^{ε3(u)}};
- N*_σ = {u : u(σ) = σ^{ε2(u)} = ε2(u)σ}.

Here ε2 and ε3 are characters with values ±1. The second form is correct because σ^{−1} = −σ.

Z_{ρ,σ} is the subgroup of elements normalizing both elements simultaneously. It is identified with M[0] ≃ Γ_Q~·L_0^Π, a semidirect ('1/2-direct') product of a copy of the Galois group by the procyclic group L_0 generated by a parabolic element. The superscript ! marks the variant attached to the free profinite group Π (π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points). Page 612 explains the difference: L_0^π has index 2 in L_0^𝔊.

The two lacets. The previous page built a central μ-extension (μ = {±1}) S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} and a canonical lifting homomorphism (117). This page says it is made explicit by the two 'canonical fundamental lacets' (118):
- a : Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N*_ρ/μ;
- b : Z_{ρ,σ} → N*_σ.

They are given by formulas (120)–(121), referring back to §51:
- a(u) = ε3[τ']α^{-1}u;
- b(u) = β^{-1}u.

Here α ∈ Π^_{0τ} and β ∈ Π^_0 are profinite paths (from the tangential base point 0 to τ, resp. loops at 0). They are characterized by u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) and u(σ) = ε2·int(β)(σ). In other words, every arithmetic automorphism moves the torsion elements ρ, σ to conjugates of themselves. The conjugating path is the 'lacet', and dividing u by it lands in the stabilizer of ρ (resp. σ).

Equivalent congruences (122): u ≡ b mod Π_0^ and u ≡ ε3[σ]a mod Π^. The page breaks off on a commutativity statement modulo 𝔊^{+^}. Page 612 then composes a and b with maps δ_ρ, δ_σ to γ_{ρ,σ} ≃ Γ_Q~ (diagram 123).

Modern reading. This is the step in the GT-type description of Galois action on the modular/braid tower where an automorphism is encoded by the conjugating elements for the order-2 and order-3 torsion. These are the analogues of the parameter f in Drinfeld's (λ, f) and of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations: the 'équation des lacets'. The marginal note itself admits the description is 'not really explicit' but an explicitation of earlier theorems.
errors: In (118) the second map is written with source Z_{ρ,σ} (no '!') while the first has Z^!_{ρ,σ}. Grothendieck himself flags this Z versus Z^! confusion on the next page ('Il serait temps de rectifier la confusion (p. 594')').
In (121) 'ε2(σ)' should presumably read ε2(u): the sign depends on the automorphism u, not on σ.

The marginal note concedes the formulas are not genuinely explicit; the characterization of α, β is only up to centralizers, hence the quotient by μ for a. This is not a mathematical error, but well-definedness depends on the earlier choices (τ', §51).

ideas.what: Encoding an arithmetic automorphism of SL(2,Z)^ (or of the profinite π1 of M_{1,1}) by the profinite elements conjugating the torsion elements ρ (order 3/6) and σ (order 4) back to their powers. These are the 'lacets', and they satisfy the 'équation des lacets'.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller parameters (λ, f) and the 2-cycle/3-cycle relations; Ihara/Drinfeld description of Galois action on Π = π1(P^1−{0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s); Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura–Schneps for the M_{1,1}/SL2 version
ideas.where_published: Spirit sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). Detailed treatment only in the unpublished Longue Marche follow-up notes (cote 140).

ideas.what: Z_{ρ,σ} ≃ M[0] ≃ Γ_Q~·L_0 as a semidirect product of a Galois section by the procyclic parabolic subgroup. The ! variant has index 2 in the parabolic part.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition group/stabilizer of a tangential base point (cusp) in the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}

ideas.what: Central μ = {±1} extension S_0Γ^! and a canonical lift expressed through the two lacets.
ideas.modern_name: Central extension by −1 ∈ SL2 of the PSL2 picture (the M_{1,1} versus orbifold P^1 with points of orders 2 and 3)

deep.surprise_reason: Bookkeeping page in the long 'équation des lacets' computation: it restates the definitions of the two canonical lacets from §51 as congruences. The underlying idea (Galois action on the modular group encoded by paths conjugating the order-2 and order-3 torsion) is Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld version of the GT relations. That precedence is already known in outline, and this specific page adds no new finished result.
transcription_corrections: (121) reads u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ), u(σ) = ε2(·) int(β)(σ): 'int' (inner automorphism), not 'i_{-α}'.
The second arrow of (118) has source Z_{ρ,σ} (no !) in the image.
Margin reads approximately: 'à dire vrai ceci n'est pas explicite, mais une explicitation des [?] théorèmes...'.
The page number at the bottom left is 611.
The last lines read approximately: 'qui impliquent a fortiori (vu dévissage[?] mod 𝔊^{+^}) ... commutativité de ...'.
